raw.description: Hardcoded secret in JWT token generation. The secret should be stored securely and not hardcoded in the source code.
raw.exploit: An attacker could potentially gain access to the JWT secret and forge tokens.

raw.description: CSRF protection is not applied to the login route. This could allow an attacker to perform actions on behalf of an authenticated user.
raw.exploit: An attacker could trick a user into visiting a malicious site that performs a login request on their behalf.

raw.description: JWT token is stored in a cookie without the Secure flag, making it vulnerable to theft over an unencrypted connection.
raw.exploit: An attacker on the same network could intercept the token if transmitted over HTTP.

raw.description: Potential SQL Injection vulnerability if the database library does not properly handle parameterized queries.
raw.exploit: If the database library is not secure, an attacker could inject SQL commands through the input fields.

raw.description: No validation of SSL/TLS certificates when making requests to the backend.
raw.exploit: An attacker could perform a man-in-the-middle attack by intercepting the requests.
